clue.text: Carla goes round eastern sultanate

indicators.note: Carla's surname encircles the letter for eastern, so it is a container signal

parts.note: Carla Bruni, singer and former model, wife of French president Sarkozy
E is the standard abbreviation for east or eastern

explanation.surface: A woman named Carla travels around an Eastern monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: Carla is Carla Bruni, the singer married to former French president Nicolas Sarkozy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small state on Borneo ruled by a sultan, so it is an example of a sultanate.

clue.text: Yielding ape or rigid rodent

indicators.note: yielding means giving way or bending, so the rigid letters are made to bend into a new order

explanation.surface: An ape that gives way, or else an unbending rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yielding' looks like it describes the ape, but it signals rearranging APE OR RIGID.
explanation.definitionFit: The prairie dog is a burrowing North American ground squirrel, so it is a kind of rodent.

clue.text: Plot to enclose land that's spoilt

indicators.note: the bed letters surround the other piece, signalling a container

parts.note: a garden bed is a plot of ground
to light is to land or settle, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: A scheme to fence off ground that has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' reads as a scheme but is a flower bed; 'land' is a verb meaning come down, alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighted crops are ruined by disease, so the word serves as a synonym for spoilt.

clue.text: Brown wading bird one missed initially? There he goes!

indicators.note: the numeral for one is dropped from the front of the bird, a deletion at the start

parts.note: the ibis is a long-legged wading bird
one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: the word he leaves the word There, so it is a deletion signal

parts.note: taken as the letters H and E

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a brown wader they nearly missed, and cries out as it flies off.
explanation.walkthrough: IBIS without its first I gives BIS; THERE once HE goes gives TRE. 'There he goes!' reads as an exclamation, but it is a deletion instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Bistre is a brownish pigment made from soot, so it names a shade of brown.

clue.text: He is held up by more audacious viewer

indicators.note: the word for more audacious holds the turned piece inside it

parts.note: bolder means more audacious

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as the letters H and E

explanation.surface: A man is delayed by someone braver than he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' looks like 'delayed', but it is two signals: 'up' turns the piece over in this down clue, and 'held' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A beholder is one who looks at something, so it is a synonym for viewer, as in beauty in the eye of the beholder.

clue.text: Saint taking Viagra, prepared to wander aimlessly in Scotland

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so the drug's letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A saint on Viagra is ready to roam aimlessly around Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is only a link joining the saint to the rearranged VIAGRA (RAVAIG).
explanation.definitionFit: Stravaig is a Scots word for roaming about idly, so it is the regional term for wandering aimlessly.

clue.text: Underwear that is covered with fine flowers

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is sits inside, covered by the other letters

parts.note: flowers here means things that flow, and rills are small streams
IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Lingerie that is printed all over with delicate flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' is not blooms but things that flow, little streams.
explanation.definitionFit: Frillies is an informal word for frilly women's knickers, so they are a kind of underwear.

clue.text: Unemployed member of comedy team

definitions.meaning: Eric of that surname was one of the Monty Python team

explanation.surface: An out-of-work member of a comedy troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Idle was a member of the Monty Python team.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means not working, and Eric Idle was a member of Monty Python's comedy team.

clue.text: Annoyed fly may be heard

indicators.note: the word for fly is spoken, and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: to soar is to fly high

explanation.surface: An irritated insect buzzing within earshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like the insect but is the verb: SOAR, which sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore is an informal synonym for annoyed or resentful, as in feeling sore about a slight.

clue.text: Taking on leads for Heaton's indie band

indicators.note: the leading letters of the two following words are taken

parts.note: a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: Someone recruiting members for Heaton's independent rock group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' reads as a group of musicians but is a circular band, a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiring means employing, so it is a synonym for taking on staff.

clue.text: Remarkable, as sheep but not goats may be

definitions.text: as sheep but not goats may be
definitions.meaning: the noun sheep can refer to one animal, whereas goats is only plural

explanation.surface: Something striking about sheep that goats never manage.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is grammar: 'sheep' can be one animal, but 'goats' always means more than one.
explanation.definitionFit: Singular means strikingly unusual, and in grammar refers to one item, which sheep can be but goats cannot.

clue.text: A moist Nigella?

parts.note: Nigella is the plant genus whose common name is a phrase about affection inside damp air; a moist one is pictured wrapped in fog

explanation.surface: A question about the TV cook Nigella Lawson being damp.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigella is not the cook but the garden flower genus; 'moist' points to damp air, a mist, around the flower's common name.
explanation.definitionFit: Love-in-a-mist is the common name of Nigella damascena, a garden flower, and a mist is moist air.

clue.text: Manage a wedding centre, one in church

indicators.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter word wedding is taken
the numeral sits inside the word for church

parts.note: a minster is a large church
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Organise a wedding venue, with someone officiating in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of WEDDING is D; one inside MINSTER makes MINISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer something is to run or manage it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Black Prince with more grey matter

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Prince Rainier III ruled Monaco and married Grace Kelly

explanation.surface: The Black Prince, Edward of Woodstock, described as cleverer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black Prince' looks like the medieval Edward, but it splits into B and Prince Rainier of Monaco.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey matter is informal for brains or intelligence, so having more of it means being cleverer.

clue.text: Is a substitute to tolerate wrongdoing?

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Is putting up with misbehaviour just a poor replacement?
explanation.definitionFit: To stand in for someone is to deputise or take their place, so the phrasal verb means acting as a replacement.

clue.text: Remark by Wilde, perhaps, on English livestock?

parts.note: a pig is a farm animal, part of the livestock
a ram is a male sheep, also livestock

explanation.surface: A witty line from Oscar Wilde about English farm animals.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'livestock', supplies two animals: PIG and RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was famous for short witty sayings, and such a pithy remark is called an epigram.

clue.text: Wine to accompany beef for pilot

parts.note: red is short for red wine
a baron of beef is a large joint of two sirloins

explanation.surface: Choosing a wine to go with a beef dish for an aviator.
explanation.walkthrough: A baron of beef is a large British roasting joint. The Red Baron was Manfred von Richthofen, the German World War I flying ace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Baron was the nickname of the famous German fighter ace of the First World War, an example of a pilot.

clue.text: Queen held by another has time for French philosopher

indicators.note: the royal cipher is held inside the name of the second queen

parts.note: Dido, Queen of Carthage, is another queen
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch is captured by a rival queen who is biding her time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another queen: Dido of Carthage, who holds ER (Elizabeth Regina).
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot edited the Encyclopédie and was a leading Enlightenment thinker, an example of a French philosopher.

clue.text: Calumny? Snarl and ignore it

indicators.note: to snarl is to tangle, so the letters are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: Faced with slander, growl and then pay it no attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snarl' looks like a growl but means tangle, rearranging AND IGNORE IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Denigration is the act of belittling someone unfairly, a synonym for calumny or slander.

clue.text: Attention-seeker with sailors in battle

indicators.note: the navy abbreviation goes inside the attention-seeking cough

parts.note: ahem is the cough used to attract attention
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: A show-off and some sailors get caught up in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attention-seeker' is not a person but the throat-clearing 'ahem'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnhem was the 1944 airborne battle in the Netherlands, so the town's name stands for that battle.

clue.text: Artist employed in the mines

indicators.note: the letters are put to work inside the words that follow, signalling a hidden word

explanation.surface: A painter who once worked down the mines.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a British artist known for her unmade bed installation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracey Emin is a well-known British conceptual artist, so she is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Dutch in Germany no closer to crime

indicators.note: the closing letter of the word for crime is removed

parts.note: fraud is a crime of deception

explanation.surface: A Dutchman in Germany is no nearer to a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is not the nationality: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife, and Frau is German for wife.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney usage Dutch means a wife, and Frau is the German word for wife or married woman.

clue.text: Isle's shrouded in darkness — it's a naval base

indicators.note: the island's name is wrapped up inside the word for darkness

parts.note: murk is darkness or gloom
the Isle of Man, made possessive, gives Man's

explanation.surface: An island lies hidden in gloom; it is a military port.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is the island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Murmansk is the Russian Arctic port that hosts the Northern Fleet, an example of a naval base.

clue.text: Tomfoolery? Not for heads of Civil Service

parts.note: anti means against, the opposite of for

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words that follow are taken

explanation.surface: Larking about? Not something the top civil servants approve of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads of Civil Service' looks like senior mandarins but gives only C and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Antics are silly or playful capers, so the word is a synonym for tomfoolery.

clue.text: Uncommon sense about our treatment for emotional disorders

indicators.note: the rearranged sense goes about, around, the other rearrangement
uncommon sense plays on common sense, the word sense being made unusual by rearranging
the word our is given treatment, worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Unusual good sense about how we treat emotional disorders.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams: 'Uncommon' gives NESES and 'treatment' gives URO, which 'about' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuroses are mild mental illnesses marked by anxiety or obsession, so they are emotional disorders.

clue.text: Bird that's born within West Bank city

indicators.note: the letter for born goes inside the bird's name

parts.note: the heron is a long-legged wading bird
B is the abbreviation for born, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A bird hatched inside a city on the West Bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebron is a Palestinian city in the West Bank, home of the Tomb of the Patriarchs.
